sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Learn Claude Code is a hands-on course in harness engineering: building the code around a language model that turns it into a working coding agent, using Claude Code's design as the model. It has 17 lessons, each adding one mechanism with runnable Python.
sixtySeconds.problem: Many agent tutorials wire LLM calls into rigid workflows. This course argues that the model provides the intelligence and your job is the harness (tools, knowledge, context, permissions), and teaches each part step by step from a single agent loop.
whoFor: Developers building their own coding agents
Engineers curious how Claude Code works inside
Python programmers learning tool use and agent loops
Readers of English, Chinese or Japanese
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it to understand agent harnesses from first principles with small runnable examples. It uses the Anthropic API, so running the code needs an API key.
requirements: Optional: Node.js for the web platform

overview: The course starts from one loop: send messages to the model, run any tools it asks for, append the results and repeat until it stops. Each lesson then adds one mechanism around that loop without rewriting it.

The 17 lessons cover the agent loop, tool use, permissions, hooks, planning with a todo list, subagents, on-demand skill loading, context compaction, memory, a file-backed task system, background tasks, a cron scheduler, agent teams with task-bound worktrees, MCP plugins, an integrated harness, a workflow runtime and a goal loop with an independent evaluator.

Each chapter folder has an English README with Chinese and Japanese translations, a standalone code.py and diagrams. A web platform lets you read lessons with source, simulator and architecture views. An older 12-lesson track is kept in docs/ and agents/ for existing links.

strengths: Builds up from a single loop
Covers advanced topics like teams and compaction
limitations: Educational code, not a production agent
Needs an Anthropic API key, which costs money per use
Two tracks exist; don't mix chapter numbers between them
Strongly opinionated about what counts as an agent
